chapter: Precision, the union and learning to read
title: Sy Oliver wrote out drum parts as a guide
summary: Crawford says Sy Oliver wrote a drum part for everyone with accents marked, which taught him he had to read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: -- musical. But, now, you said a little earlier that you had been reading (drum) parts that --
But, now, that's what I was trying to find out a little bit earlier, when you were saying that Sy Oliver had parts for you.
Did he tell you what he wanted you to play, or did he write down --
He wrote it down on music paper.

Wrote it down, because Sy Oliver was a staunch believer in playing what he wanted to play. Phrasing-wise and playing. Now, he would write me a drum part, and everybody in that band, he would write it. That's what he wanted you to play.

That was a guide, like, a guide sheet. Music is nothing for drums but mathematics, adding and subtraction, and all that kind of -- that's all, just straight time, and then if he wants you to accent something, then he'd put a mark over it, where you knew what to do. Catch this and that, write it,

verbally and musically. And then when I first started to realizing that I really had to read, no more going by ear, which I was great at that. That's why I say, you got to know how to play the blues. Then you can get a lot of education from the blues.
